Accessibility of PrairieLearn Content

This is the report for the course’s PrairieLearn content. See also the accessibility overview and the report for the course website.

Accessibility Statement

Quizzes, labs, homeworks, and the final project for IS445 (Data Visualization) are delivered through PrairieLearn. This page documents how the assessments and questions we have written for PrairieLearn measure up against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Levels A and AA, including the places where they fall short.

If any assessment is a barrier for you, please contact the instructor at jnaiman@illinois.edu. You do not need to wait for a fix: we will provide the assessment in a form that works for you.

Conformance Report

This report follows the structure of the VPAT® 2.4Rev WCAG edition.

   
Name of product IS445 Data Visualization assessments on PrairieLearn, Fall 2026, section BU
Location Course instance Fa26BU in the pl-is445 course repository (access is limited to course staff)
Report date November 2026
Description 50 assessments that together use 183 questions: quizzes, labs, homeworks, extra credit, the final project, and ungraded in-class workspaces.
Contact Jill Naiman, jnaiman@illinois.edu
Standard WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA

Scope

The report covers the content the course staff wrote: the question text, figures, tables, and answer inputs of every question used by an assessment in this course instance, and the starter notebooks that open in workspaces.

It does not cover the PrairieLearn platform itself (page layout, navigation, the standard question elements, grading messages). PrairieLearn publishes its own conformance report, and where a criterion is decided by the platform, the remarks below say so. It also does not cover the JupyterLab and VS Code applications that run inside workspaces, beyond the notes in the Workspaces table.

Evaluation methods

Every assessment in courseInstances/Fa26BU/assessments was traced to the questions it uses, and the source of each of those 183 questions (question.html, info.json, server.py, and workspace notebooks) was reviewed. The questions break down as follows: 83 multiple choice, 25 checkbox, 7 dropdown, 6 drag-and-drop ordering, 3 matching, 45 workspace, 14 with hand-written form controls, and a small number of text, number, and file-upload questions.

The following have not yet been done, and ratings may change once they are:

  • opening each question in PrairieLearn as a student;
  • testing with a screen reader or with the keyboard only;
  • checking captions on linked recordings;
  • reviewing randomly generated variants of questions beyond their templates;
  • evaluating the workspace applications.

Terms

The terms used in the “Conformance level” column are defined as follows:

  • Supports: the content has at least one method that meets the criterion without known defects, or meets it with equivalent facilitation.
  • Partially Supports: some content does not meet the criterion.
  • Does Not Support: the majority of the content does not meet the criterion.
  • Not Applicable: the criterion is not relevant to the content.

Status

The “Status” column in each table tracks our progress on that criterion. Each entry lists the questions to look at. Links go to the question’s folder in the course repository, and the link text is its path under questions/.

  • To do a known problem that nobody has started fixing. In the tables, write s="todo".
  • In progress a fix has been started but is not finished. Write s="progress".
  • Needs check no known problem, but the rating has not been confirmed by testing. Write s="check".
  • Done fixed or confirmed. Write s="done".
  • No action nothing to do. Write s="none".
